answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation system anchored to a proof-of-stake (PoS) mechanism, leveraging a "lotus" of validator nodes that require a bonded stake, similar to a marble deposited in a secure vault. An attacker attempting a Sybil attack would need to acquire and lock a substantial amount of stake, akin to trying to entwine a vast network with a fragile vine, making it economically infeasible to create multiple fake identities. The cost of such an attack would be prohibitively expensive, thereby securing the network.
